references.text: Elijah prophesied that there would be no rain or dew in Israel, which initiated the three-and-a-half-year drought Jesus refers to.
The brook Cherith dried up because of the drought, confirming the great famine Jesus mentions.
There was a severe famine in Samaria, which aligns with Jesus' reference to the great famine throughout the land.
Elijah was sent to a widow in Zarephath in Sidon—this is the specific event Jesus refers to in his speech, where Elijah was sent to a foreign widow instead of the many widows in Israel.
James refers to the same event: Elijah prayed, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months; then he prayed again, and heaven gave rain.
The two witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain falls, an allusion to Elijah's ministry and the closed sky Jesus mentions.
God can close the sky so that no rain comes, but promises to hear his people if they humble themselves—this principle underlies the event Jesus describes.
A warning that God may close the sky so that no rain falls if the people turn away—the background for the drought in Elijah's time.
